body:
Today's scan turned up zero cross-platform arbitrage opportunities. That's not surprising once you look at what's actually being compared: Kalshi's gold contracts are settlement markets that pay out based on where spot gold lands at a specific future moment (year-end or a September 30 close), while Polymarket's contracts are mostly touch markets that pay out if gold ever hits a level at any point during a window, regardless of where it ends up. A settle-above-$4,300 contract and a touch-$4,300 contract on the same underlying can have very different fair prices even when gold is trading right near that line, so the scanner correctly isn't flagging the overlap as free money.

Gold itself is the real story right now. Spot has been trading in the $4,370-$4,420 range this week, with gold pushing above $4,390 an ounce on Wednesday, supported by a weaker US dollar as investors weighed inflation risk from Middle East tensions ahead of key US inflation data. That backdrop shows up clearly in the strikes: Kalshi's year-end 4,300 or above contract is bid at 68 cents and its 4,400 or above contract at 57 cents, pricing in a market that already sees itself comfortably past both thresholds with room to spare into December. Polymarket's September touch $4,500 contract, at 75-76 cents, reflects the same expectation that a level not far above today's price is a good bet to be touched before month-end, not any strange mispricing.

Volume is thin on several of the far out-of-the-money Kalshi strikes (a number show zero 24-hour volume), which is a reminder that quoted bid-ask spreads there may not reflect what you could actually trade at size. Nothing today looks like a genuine cross-platform edge; the apparent gaps between similar-sounding strikes are explained by the settle-versus-touch difference in contract design rather than any pricing error.
headline: No cross-platform gold arbitrage today -- settle vs touch contracts explain the gaps
